Dear Secretary Reese:

        Pursuant to Section 205 of the Federal Power Act (“FPA”) 1 and Section 35.13 of the
regulations of the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission (“FERC” or “Commission”), 2
Portland General Electric Company (“PGE” or the “Company”) hereby submits for filing
revisions to the transmission rates contained in its Open Access Transmission Tariff (“OATT” or
“Tariff”), as well as other limited revisions to its OATT. 3 PGE proposes to implement cost-
based formula rates for transmission service under Schedule 1 (Scheduling, System Control and
Dispatch Service), Schedule 7 (Long-Term Firm and Short-Term Firm Point-to-Point
Transmission Service), Schedule 8 (Non-Firm Point-to-Point Transmission Service) (Schedules 7
and 8 referred to herein as “PTP” service), and Attachment H (Annual Transmission Revenue
Requirement for Network Integration Transmission Service (“NITS”)) taken under its OATT.
The proposed Attachment H will include a formula rate, consisting of a formula rate template
(“Template”) (Attachment H-1), implementation protocols (“Protocols”) (Attachment H-2), and
depreciation and amortization rates (Attachment H-3) (together, “Formula Rate”), to determine
the rates for, and recover the costs of, PGE’s investment in transmission facilities.

       PGE submits that the proposed Formula Rate and limited OATT revisions are just and
reasonable, not unduly discriminatory or preferential, and should be accepted without condition,
modification, hearing, or suspension. PGE requests that the Commission accept for filing the
proposed Formula Rate and limited OATT revisions to be effective January 1, 2027. 4

I.      BACKGROUND

        A.         Portland General Electric Company

        PGE is a regulated, vertically integrated electric utility located in the Western Electricity
Coordinating Council region. It provides electric service to over 960,000 residential,
commercial, and industrial customers across seven counties and 51 Oregon cities. PGE’s service
territory spans approximately 4,000 square miles, stretching from Grand Ronde and Yamhill
County east to Mount Hood, and from the Portland metropolitan area south to Salem. PGE owns
generation, transmission, and distribution facilities for service to wholesale and retail customers,
and it buys and sells power in the Western energy markets. PGE’s all-time net system peak load
reached 4,498 MW on August 16, 2023. PGE’s generation capacity includes a diverse mix of
wind, natural gas-fired combined cycles, hydroelectric, coal, and other resources, including those
obtained through power purchase agreements. PGE solely owns and operates 1,269 circuit miles
of transmission and is a joint owner of certain other transmission paths in the Northwest. PGE
maintains over 50 different points of interconnection with other utilities at the transmission and
sub-transmission levels. PGE is subject to the regulatory authority of the Oregon Public Utility
Commission (“OPUC”) for its Oregon utility operations, and to the jurisdiction of FERC for the
sale of electricity at wholesale and transmission services in interstate commerce.

        B.         PGE’s Current Stated Transmission Rates

        PGE’s current stated transmission rates were established pursuant to an uncontested
settlement resolving all issues set for hearing and settlement judge procedures by the
Commission in Docket No. ER22-233-000 as part of PGE’s last transmission rate case, effective
January 1, 2022 (“2022 Settlement”).5 There, PGE proposed OATT revisions to increase its
transmission rates for service under Schedule 1, Schedule 7, Schedule 8, and Attachment H.
PGE proposed an annual transmission revenue requirement (“ATRR”) under Attachment H of
$91.4 million, but settled with customers for a “black box” ATRR amount of $81.403 million. 6
The 2022 Settlement also provided that PGE’s depreciation rate will be a 2.00% composite
annual depreciation rate.7 The 2022 Settlement further required PGE to make an FPA section
205 filing with the Commission to update its Schedule 1, Schedule 7, Schedule 8, and
Attachment H rates to be effective no later than January 1, 2027. 8

         C.        Changes Since PGE’s Last Rate Case

        PGE recently reclassified, with OPUC and Commission approval, certain 57 kV facilities
as transmission because they function as part of PGE’s integrated transmission network. 9 On
September 27, 2024, PGE filed an application requesting approval from the OPUC for the
reclassification of 57 kV facilities to transmission.10 On February 12, 2025, PGE and parties in
the OPUC proceeding reached a settlement, in the form of an uncontested stipulation, in which
the stipulating parties agreed not to object to the reclassification of the 57 kV facilities. On
March 14, 2025, the OPUC adopted the stipulation, finding that its terms were supported by
sufficient evidence, appropriately resolved the issues in that case, and contributed to an overall
settlement in the public interest. 11 Shortly thereafter, on March 19, 2025, PGE filed a petition for
a declaratory order with the Commission seeking a determination that the same 57 kV facilities
are transmission assets and, therefore, Commission-jurisdictional. 12 On July 2, 2025, the
Commission issued an order finding that, based on its application of the seven factor test, the
“Proposed 57 kV Facilities are transmission assets and thus subject to the Commission’s
jurisdiction.”13

II.      THE PROPOSED FORMULA RATE IS JUST AND REASONABLE

        PGE proposes to implement cost-based formula rates for transmission service under
Schedule 1, Schedule 7, Schedule 8, and Attachment H taken under its OATT. The Formula
Rate consists of a Template and implementation Protocols to determine and recover the costs of
PGE’s investment in transmission facilities. PGE proposes to replace its currently-effective
stated transmission rates with the Formula Rate that is incorporated into Attachment H of its
OATT.

        A.          Forward-Looking Formula Rate

        The Formula Rate is forward-looking and similar to the formula rates the Commission
has approved for other public utilities. As explained below and in the testimony of PGE’s rate
consultant Mr. John Tsoukalis, a Principal with the Brattle Group, the Formula Rate filed
herewith establishes a forward-looking formula that recovers projected transmission costs on a
calendar-year basis, i.e., the twelve consecutive month period that begins on January 1 and
continues through December 31 (“Rate Year”), with an annual true-up (inclusive of interest at
Commission-published quarterly interest rates) to ensure that only actual costs and a reasonable
return on investment are collected from customers. 14 PGE will use the projected net
transmission revenue requirement (“PTRR”) to calculate the transmission rates to be effective
each Rate Year beginning on January 1.15 The true-up between the PTRR and PGE’s actual
ATRR will then be calculated the following year and applied, with interest, as an addition to or
subtraction from the subsequent year’s PTRR. 16 This true-up mechanism ensures that the
transmission rates charged to customers include only the actual costs incurred, no more, no
less.17

        Mr. Tsoukalis explains that the Template will identify the data to be used in the revenue
requirement calculation. For the actual ATRR, the Template will be populated with cost data
that comes primarily from PGE’s FERC Form No. 1, which is filed annually with the
Commission. In contrast, data used to calculate the PTRR will come from a mix of historical
and projected account balances. 18 PGE will project additions to plant, including a
complementary projection of depreciation and accumulated deferred income taxes (“ADIT”), as
well as load.19

(1) rate calculation; (2) rate base; (3) excess/deficient income taxes (“EDIT”); and (4)
expenses.20 The rate calculation section includes the development of the revenue requirement
and final transmission rate and Schedule 1 rate calculations, including the cost of capital, income
taxes, load divisor, and true-up. PGE will compute the revenue requirement on Table 2 of the

        PGE will calculate its PTRR using a mix of historical and projected account balances. 28
PGE intends to project values for plant, depreciation, ADIT, and load, as these are the accounts
for which PGE maintains forecasts.29 For plant and depreciation, PGE will project monthly
account balances for transmission plant accounts and their associated accumulated depreciation
based on expected capital spending, projected in-service timelines for planned facilities, and
expected depreciation and retirement of existing facilities. The PTRR will include PGE’s
expected 13-month average balance of transmission plant and transmission accumulated
depreciation. In regard to ADIT, PGE will forecast ADIT based on the expected tax impact of
planned transmission plant additions and will prorate the associated portion of depreciation-
related ADIT consistent with Internal Revenue Service normalization requirements. ADIT
activity that is not subject to the proration requirement will be averaged rather than prorated.
Lastly, PGE will forecast the load used to calculate rates charged to customers based on PGE’s
projections for native NITS load, historical load for non-native NITS, and all other transmission
service loads.30 Short-term firm PTP, and non-firm PTP service are excluded from the load
divisor calculation because revenues from these services are accounted for in the revenue
requirement calculation as revenue credits. 31

        PGE’s true-up mechanism will calculate the true-up on a two-year rolling basis,
consistent with other Commission-approved formula rates. 32 Each year, PGE will calculate the
difference between the revenue collected based on projected rates and the revenue that should
have been collected based on the actual ATRR from that year using FERC Form 1 data. PGE
will calculate any over- or under-collection of revenues and apply the Commission’s quarterly
interest rates, and such calculated amount will be added to the following year’s PTRR. PGE’s
true-up mechanism also allows for prior period adjustments that may be required to resolve
reporting errors or settlement of any challenges from previous true-up calculations. 33

        B.          Return on Equity

        PGE requests a base ROE of 11.20%, which is supported by the testimony and analysis
of PGE’s consultant, Ms. Ann E. Bulkley, a Principal with the Brattle Group, and is consistent
with Commission Opinion No. 594.37 The Formula Rate includes a stated total base ROE value
of 11.20%, which is well within the zone of reasonableness that Ms. Bulkley developed based on
her cost of equity estimates for a national proxy group.

        According to Ms. Bulkley, Hope and Bluefield, which established the Commission’s
standards for determining a regulated company’s ROE, provide that the proper rate of return
must be: (1) adequate to attract capital on reasonable terms; (2) sufficient to ensure the
company’s financial integrity; and (3) commensurate with returns on investments in enterprises
with similar risks.38 As Ms. Bulkley explains, the ability to attract capital at reasonable terms is
important because it allows the utility to provide safe, reliable service while maintaining its
financial integrity.39 Accordingly, it is important for PGE’s ROE analysis to take into
consideration current and projected capital market conditions, as well as investors’ expectations
and requirements for both risks and returns. 40 If investors do not expect current market
conditions to be sustained in the future, it is possible that the cost of equity estimation models
will not provide an accurate estimate of investors’ required return. 41 Therefore, it is important to
consider capital market conditions to assess utility investor expectations.

III.    OATT REVISIONS

     As part of this filing, PGE proposes to revise certain Schedules and Attachments in its
OATT to implement the Formula Rate.

        A.         Schedule 1

        PGE is proposing to implement a formula rate mechanism for Schedule 1 (Scheduling,
System Control and Dispatch Service). From a tariff perspective, the formula for Schedule 1
will reside in Attachment H. Accordingly, certain revisions to Schedule 1 are being proposed to
accommodate that change. First, PGE is proposing tariff revisions explaining that the charges
under Schedule 1 will be calculated in accordance with Attachment H-1 of the Tariff and
removing the list of stated annual, monthly, weekly, daily, and hourly rates. Second, language
has been added stating that such charges will be updated annually pursuant to the procedures set
forth in Attachment H-2 of the Tariff.

        B.         Schedule 7 and Schedule 8

        Similarly, PGE is proposing to implement a formula rate mechanism for Schedule 7
(Long-Term Firm and Short-Term Firm Point-to-Point Transmission Service) and Schedule 8
(Non-Firm Point-to-Point Transmission Service). As with Schedule 1, the formula for charges
under Schedules 7 and 8 will reside in Attachment H. Accordingly, PGE is revising Schedules 7
and 8 to indicate that the formula rates for these schedules will be set forth in Attachment H-1.
PGE is also making conforming changes by removing the list of stated rates from both schedules
and adding language explaining that such charges will be updated annually pursuant to the
procedures set forth in Attachment H-2 of the Tariff.

        C.         Attachment H

        To reflect the conversion from a stated rate to a formula rate for the recovery of the costs
of PGE’s investment in transmission facilities, the proposed Attachment H will include four
components: Attachment H (Title Page and short description of the NITS and Retail Network
Integration Transmission Service rate); Attachment H-1 (Template); Attachment H-2
(Protocols); and Attachment H-3 (Depreciation Rates). Accordingly, PGE proposes to revise
Attachment H to remove the stated ATRR, indicate that the revenue requirement will be
calculated pursuant to Attachment H-1, and clarify that such charges will be updated annually
pursuant to the Protocols included in Attachment H-2. Finally, PGE proposes to establish a new
Attachment H-3, which will present PGE’s depreciation rates and amortization rates. 66

                                      SCHEDULE 1

                  Scheduling, System Control and Dispatch Service

    This service is required to schedule the movement of power through, out of, within, or

into a Control Area. This service can be provided only by the operator of the Control Area

in which the transmission facilities used for transmission service are located. Scheduling,

System Control and Dispatch Service is to be provided directly by the Transmission

Provider (if the Transmission Provider is the Control Area operator) or indirectly by the

Transmission Provider making arrangements with the Control Area operator that performs

this service for the Transmission Provider’s Transmission System. The Transmission

Customer must purchase this service from the Transmission Provider or the Control Area

operator. The charges for Scheduling, System Control and Dispatch Service will be

calculated in accordance with the formula in Attachment H-1 of the Tariff. Charges for

Schedule 1 will be updated annually on January 1 of each year and will be posted on the

Transmission Provider’s OASIS in accordance with the procedures in Attachment H-2. To

the extent the Control Area operator performs this service for the Transmission Provider,

charges to the Transmission Customer are to reflect only a pass-through of the costs

charged to the Transmission Provider by that Control Area operator.
                                        SCHEDULE 7
                      Long-Term Firm and Short-Term Firm Point-To-Point
                                    Transmission Service

        The Transmission Customer shall compensate the Transmission Provider each month for

Reserved Capacity at rates “up to” the sum of the applicable charges set forth in the formula in

Attachment H-1 of the Tariff. Charges for Schedule 7 will be updated annually on January 1 of

each year and will be posted on the Transmission Provider’s OASIS in accordance with the

procedures in Attachment H-2.

        The total demand charge in any week, pursuant to a reservation for Daily delivery, shall

not exceed the rate specified in Attachment H-1 for Weekly delivery times the highest amount in

kilowatts of Reserved Capacity in any day during such week.

        1)      Discounts: Three principal requirements apply to discounts for transmission

service as follows (1) any offer of a discount made by the Transmission Provider must be

announced to all Eligible Customers solely by posting on the OASIS, (2) any customer-initiate

requests for discounts (including requests for use by one’s wholesale merchant or an Affiliate’s

use) must occur solely by posting on the OASIS, and (3) once a discount is negotiated, details must

be immediately posted on the OASIS. For any discount agreed upon for service on a path, from

point(s) of receipt to point(s) of delivery, the Transmission Provider must offer the same

discounted transmission service rate for the same time period to all Eligible Customers on all

unconstrained transmission paths that go to the same point(s) of delivery on the Transmission

System.

        2)      Resales: The rates and rules governing charges and discounts stated above shall
not apply to resales of transmission service, compensation for which shall be governed by section
23.1 of the Tariff.
        3)      Taxes: PGE may add to the above amount an amount in dollars sufficient to

reimburse PGE for any amounts paid or payable by them as sales, excise or similar taxes (other

than taxes based upon or measured by net income) in respect of the total amount payable to PGE

pursuant to this Tariff, if necessary to allow PGE, after provision for such taxes, to realize the net

amount payable to them under this Tariff. The amount of these taxes shall be detailed in the Service

Agreement which shall be filed with the Commission. If the taxes or tax rates change, then PGE

shall have the right to revise the Service Agreement and file it with the Commission.

       4)      Capacity Designations: Capacity designations at the Point(s) of Receipt will be
inclusive of transmission losses.
                                          SCHEDULE 8

                      Non-Firm Point-To-Point Transmission Service

        The Transmission Customer shall compensate the Transmission Provider for Non-

Firm Point-To-Point Transmission Service up to the sum of the applicable charges set forth

in the formula in Attachment H-1 of the Tariff. Charges for Schedule 8 will be updated

annually on January 1 of each year and will be posted on the Transmission Provider’s

OASIS in accordance with the procedures in Attachment H-2.

        The total charge in any week, pursuant to a reservation for Daily delivery, shall not

exceed the rate specified in Attachment H-1 for Weekly delivery times the highest amount

in kilowatts of Reserved Capacity in any day during such week. In addition, the total

charge in any week, pursuant to a reservation for Hourly or Daily delivery, shall not exceed

the rate specified in Attachment H-1 for Weekly delivery times the highest amount in

kilowatts of Reserved Capacity in any hour during such week.

        1)       Discounts: Three principal requirements apply to discounts for transmission

service as follows (1) any offer of a discount made by the Transmission Provider must be

announced to all Eligible Customers solely by posting on the OASIS, (2) any customer-initiated

requests for discounts (including requests for use by one’s wholesale merchant or an Affiliate’s

use) must occur solely by posting on the OASIS, and (3) once a discount is negotiated, details must

be immediately posted on the OASIS. For any discount agreed upon for service on a path, from

point(s) of receipt to point(s) of delivery, the Transmission Provider must offer the same discounted

transmission service rate for the same time period to all Eligible Customers on all unconstrained

transmission paths that go to the same point(s) of delivery on the Transmission System.

        2)       Resales: The rates and rules governing charges and discounts stated above shall
not apply to resales of transmission service, compensation for which shall be governed by section
23.1 of the Tariff.
         3)       Taxes: There shall be added to the above amount an amount in dollars sufficient

to reimburse PGE for any amounts paid or payable by them as sales, excise or similar taxes (other

than taxes based upon or measured by net income) in respect of the total amount payable to PGE

pursuant to this Tariff, if necessary to allow PGE, after provision for such taxes, to realize the net

amount payable to them under this Tariff. The amount of these taxes shall be detailed in

the Service Agreement which shall be filed with the Commission. If the taxes or tax rates

change, then PGE shall have the right to revise the Service Agreement and file it with the

Commission.

        4)       Interruption or Curtailment: A Transmission Customer reserving Short-

term Non-firm Transmission Service shall not be relieved from paying PGE the agreed

upon price unless such Non-firm service is interrupted or curtailed by PGE. In the event

service is interrupted or curtailed, PGE shall reduce the charge to the Transmission

Customer the following amounts per MW for each hour in which the use of the Reserved

Capacity is interrupted or curtailed by PGE.

         For monthly deliveries:          The monthly charge / MW ÷ 346

         For weekly deliveries:           The weekly charge / MW ÷ 80

         For daily deliveries:            The daily charge / MW ÷ 16

Such reductions shall be made for up to 16 hours of interruptions or curtailments per day,

80 hours of interruptions or curtailments per week, and up to 346 hours of interruptions or

curtailments per month.

        5)       Capacity Designations: Capacity designations at the Point(s) of Receipt

will be inclusive of transmission losses.
                                       ATTACHMENT H


                         Annual Transmission Revenue Requirement
                        For Network Integration Transmission Service



1.      Charges for Network Integration Transmission Service and Retail Network Integration
Transmission Service shall be calculated annually using the Transmission Provider’s Annual
Transmission Revenue Requirement, which is derived from Formula Rate Template set forth in
Attachment H-1. The resulting rates are posted on the Transmission Provider’s OASIS. The
charge for Network Integration Transmission Service and Retail Network Integration
Transmission Service shall be updated annually in accordance with Attachment H-2. The $/kW-
year charge divided by 12, shall be assessed to the Network Customer’s monthly Network Usage
calculated pursuant to Section 34.2 of the Tariff.

2.    The Formula Rate in Attachment H-1 shall be effective until amended by the
Transmission Provider or modified by the Commission.

3.       PGE may add to the above amount an amount in dollars sufficient to reimburse PGE for
any amounts paid or payable by them as sales, excise or similar taxes (other than taxes based
upon or measured by net income) in respect of the total amount payable to PGE pursuant to this
Tariff, if necessary to allow PGE, after provision for such taxes, to realize the net amount
payable to them under this Tariff. The amount of these taxes shall be detailed in the Service
Agreement which shall be filed with the Commission. If the taxes or tax rates change, then PGE
shall have the right to revise the Service Agreement and file it with the Commission.

4.     All quantities used in calculating the Network Customer’s Network Usage and
Transmission Provider’s Monthly Transmission System Peak shall be adjusted to the
transmission system input level, i.e., shall include the transmission capacity amount associated
with any applicable losses.

Section I.    Applicability

The following procedures shall apply to Portland General Electric Company’s (“PGE”)
calculation of its actual net transmission revenue requirement (“ATRR”), True-Up Adjustment,
and projected net transmission revenue requirement (“PTRR”).

Section II.   Annual True-Up and Projected Net Revenue Requirement

A.     On or before June 1 of each year subsequent to calendar year 2027, PGE shall
       determine its Annual True-Up pursuant to its Formula Rate template and Section VII
       of these protocols, to derive a True-Up Adjustment to be included in PGE’s PTRR for
       the subsequent calendar year (the “Rate Year”).

B.     On or before June 1 of each year subsequent to calendar year 2027, PGE shall provide its
       Annual True-Up, ATRR, and True-Up Adjustment and cause such information to be
       posted on OASIS.

C.     On or before September 1 of each year, PGE shall provide its PTRR and cause such
       information to be posted on OASIS. PGE will conduct a meeting with Interested Parties
       (as such term is defined in Section II.G of these protocols) on the PTRR for the Rate
       Year within thirty (30) days of posting. Notice of the customer meeting, including the
       time, date, and location, shall be posted on OASIS and distributed to the e-mail exploder
       list no less than seven (7) days prior to such meeting.

D.     If the date for posting the Annual True-Up or the PTRR falls on a weekend or a holiday
       recognized by FERC, then the posting shall be due on the next business day. The date on
       which posting of the Annual True-Up occurs shall be that year’s “Publication Date.” Any
       delay in the Publication Date or in the posting of the PTRR will result in an equivalent
       extension of time for the submission of Information Requests discussed in Section III of
       these protocols.

E.     The Annual True-Up shall:

        1.    Include a workable data-populated Formula Rate Template and underlying
              workpapers in native format with all formulas and links intact;

        2.    Be based on PGE’s FERC Form No. 1 for the prior calendar year;

        3.    Provide the formula rate calculations and all inputs thereto, as well as supporting
              documentation and workpapers for data that are used in the Annual True-Up that


                                               1
                are not otherwise available in the FERC Form No. 1;1

        4.     Provide sufficient information to enable Interested Parties (as that term is defined
               in Section II.G of these protocols) to replicate the calculation of the Annual True-
               Up results from the FERC Form No. 1;

        5.     Identify any changes in the formula references (page and line numbers) to the
               FERC Form No. 1;

        6.     Identify all adjustments made to the FERC Form No. 1 data in determining
               formula inputs, including relevant footnotes to the FERC Form No. 1 and any
               material adjustments not shown in the FERC Form No. 1;

        7.     Provide underlying data for formula rate inputs that provide greater granularity
               than is required for the FERC Form No. 1;

        8.     With respect to any change in accounting that affects inputs to the formula rate or
               the resulting charges billed under the formula rate (“Accounting Change”):

               a.      Identify Accounting Changes, including:

                       i.     The initial implementation of an accounting standard or policy;

                       ii.    the initial implementation of accounting practices for unusual or
                              unconventional items where FERC has not provided specific
                              accounting direction;

                       iii.   correction of errors and prior period adjustments that impact the
                              True-Up Adjustment calculation;

                       iv.    the implementation of new estimation methods or policies
                              that change prior estimates; and

                       v.     changes to income tax elections;

               b.      Identify items included in the Annual True-Up at an amount other than on
                       a historic cost basis (e.g., fair value adjustments);

               c.      Identify any reorganization or merger transaction during the previous year
                       and explain the effect of the accounting for such transaction(s) on inputs to

1
        It is the intent of the formula rate, including the supporting explanations and allocations
described therein, that each input to the formula rate will be either taken directly from the FERC
Form No. 1 or reconcilable to the FERC Form No. 1 by the application of clearly identified and
supported information. If the referenced form is superseded, the successor form(s) shall be
utilized and supplemented as necessary to provide equivalent information as that provided in the
superseded form. If the referenced form(s) is (are) discontinued, equivalent information as that
provided in the discontinued form(s) shall be utilized.
                                                 2
                   the Annual True-Up;

           d.     Provide, for each item identified pursuant to items II.E.8.a - II.E.8.c of
                  these protocols, a narrative explanation of the individual impact of such
                  changes on the True-Up Adjustment.

     9.    Include for the applicable Rate Year the following information related to affiliate
           cost allocation: (A) a detailed description of the methodologies used to allocate
           and directly assign costs between PGE and its affiliates by service category and
           function, including any changes to such cost allocation methodologies from the
           prior year, and the reasons and justification for those changes; and (B) the
           magnitude of such costs that have been allocated or directly assigned between
           PGE and each affiliate by service category or function.

F.   The PTRR shall:

     1.    Include a workable data-populated Formula Rate Template and underlying
           workpapers in native format with all formulas and links intact;

     2.    Provide the formula rate calculations and all inputs thereto, as well as supporting
           documentation and workpapers for data that are used in the PTRR;

     3.    Provide sufficient information to enable Interested Parties (as that term is defined
           in Section II.G of these protocols) to replicate the calculation of the PTRR;

     4.    With respect to any Accounting Change:

           a.     Identify any Accounting Changes, including

                  i.      The initial implementation of an accounting standard or policy;

                  ii.     the initial implementation of accounting practices for unusual
                          or unconventional items where FERC has not provided specific
                          accounting direction;

                  iii.    correction of errors and prior period adjustments that impact the
                          PTRR;

                  iv.     the implementation of new estimation methods or policies that
                          change prior estimates; and

                  v.      changes to income tax elections;

           b.     Identify items included in the PTRR at an amount other than on a historic
                  cost basis (e.g., fair value adjustments);

           c.     Identify any reorganization or merger transaction during the previous year
                  and explain the effect of the accounting for such transaction(s) on inputs to
                                             3
                       the PTRR;

              d.      Provide, for each item identified pursuant to items II.F.4.a - II.F.4.c of
                      these protocols, a narrative explanation of the individual impact of
                      such changes on the PTRR.

G.     PGE shall hold an open meeting among Interested Parties (“Annual True-Up Meeting”)
       between the Publication Date and July 15. No less than seven (7) days prior to such
       Annual True-Up Meeting, PGE shall provide notice on OASIS of the time, date, and
       location of the Annual True-Up Meeting. PGE shall allow Interested Parties to access
       such meeting remotely. For purposes of these procedures, the term Interested Party
       includes, but is not limited to, customers under the Tariff, state utility regulatory
       commissions, consumer advocacy agencies, and state attorneys general. The Annual
       True-Up Meeting shall (i) permit PGE to explain and clarify its Annual True-Up and
       True-Up Adjustment and (ii) provide Interested Parties an opportunity to seek
       information and clarifications from PGE about the Annual True-Up and True-Up
       Adjustment.

H.     PGE shall hold an open meeting among Interested Parties (“Annual Projected Rate
       Meeting”) between the date that the PTRR is posted to OASIS (as described in Section
       II.C of these protocols) and September 30. No less than seven (7) days prior to such
       Annual Projected Rate Meeting, PGE shall provide notice on OASIS of the time, date,
       and location of the Annual Projected Rate Meeting. PGE shall allow Interested Parties to
       access such meeting remotely. The Annual Projected Rate Meeting shall (i) permit PGE
       to explain and clarify its PTRR and (ii) provide Interested Parties an opportunity to seek
       information and clarifications from PGE about the PTRR.

I.     Transmission owners with transmission projects that utilize a regional or inter-regional
       cost sharing mechanism will endeavor to hold a joint informational meeting to enable all
       interested parties to understand how those Transmission owners are implementing their
       formula rates for cost recovery of such projects. Such meeting shall occur by October 15
       of each year (or the next business day if October 15 falls on a weekend or holiday
       recognized by FERC). Notice of joint informational meetings, including the time, date,
       and location, shall be posted on OASIS no less than seven (7) days prior to such
       meetings.

Section III. Information Exchange Procedures

Each Annual True-Up and PTRR shall be subject to the following information exchange
procedures (“Information Exchange Procedures”):

A.     Interested Parties shall have until December 1 following Publication Date (unless such
       period is extended with the written consent of PGE or by FERC order) to serve
       reasonable information and document requests on PGE related to the Annual True-Up
       and the PTRR (“Information Exchange Period”). If December 1 falls on a weekend or a
       holiday recognized by FERC, the deadline for submitting all information and document
       requests shall be extended to the next business day. Such information and document
       requests shall be limited to what is necessary to determine:
                                                 4
       1.      the extent or effect of an Accounting Change;

      2.      whether the Annual True-Up or PTRR fails to include data properly recorded in
              accordance with these protocols;

      3.      the proper application of the formula rate and procedures in these protocols;

      4.      the accuracy of data and consistency with the formula rate of the calculations
              shown in the Annual True-Up or PTRR;

      5.      the prudence of actual costs and expenditures included in the Annual True-Up and
              PTRR;

      6.      the effect of any change to the underlying Uniform System of Accounts or FERC
              Form No. 1;

      7.      the prudence of procurement methods and cost control methodologies bearing on
              the Annual True-Up and PTRR; or

      8.      any other information that may reasonably have substantive effect on the
              calculation of the Annual True-Up or PTRR pursuant to the formula.

      The information and document requests shall not otherwise be directed to ascertaining
      whether the formula rate is just and reasonable.

B.    PGE shall make a good faith effort to respond to information and document requests
      within fifteen (15) business days of receipt of such requests. PGE shall respond to all
      information and document requests by no later than January 15 following the
      Publication Date, unless the Information Exchange Period is extended by PGE or
      FERC.

C.    PGE shall post on OASIS all information requests from Interested Parties and PGE’s
      response(s) to such requests; except, however, if responses to information and document
      requests include material deemed by PGE to be confidential information, such
      information will not be publicly posted but will be made available to requesting parties
      pursuant to a confidentiality agreement to be executed by PGE and the requesting party.

D.    PGE shall not claim that responses to information and document requests provided
      pursuant to these protocols are subject to any settlement privilege in any subsequent
      FERC proceeding addressing PGE’s Annual True-Up or PTRR.

Section IV.   Challenge Procedures

A.    Interested Parties shall have until January 31 following the Publication Date (unless such
      period is extended with the written consent of PGE or by FERC order) to review the
      inputs, supporting explanations, allocations and calculations and to notify PGE in writing,
      which may be made electronically, of any specific Informal Challenges to the Annual
      True-Up or PTRR. The period of time from the Publication Date until January 31 shall be
                                               5
      referred to as the “Review Period.” If January 31 falls on a weekend or a holiday
     recognized by FERC, the deadline for submitting all Informal Challenges shall be
     extended to the next business day. Failure to pursue an issue through an Informal
     Challenge or to lodge a Formal Challenge regarding any issue as to a given Annual True-
     Up or PTRR shall bar pursuit of such issue with respect to that Annual True-Up or
     PTRR, but shall not bar pursuit of such issue or the lodging of a Formal Challenge as to
     such issue as it relates to a subsequent Annual True-Up or PTRR.

B.   A party submitting an Informal Challenge to PGE must specify the inputs, supporting
     explanations, allocations, calculations, or other information to which it objects, and
     provide an appropriate explanation and documents to support its challenge. PGE shall
     make a good faith effort to respond to any Informal Challenge within twenty (20)
     business days of notification of such challenge. PGE shall appoint a senior representative
     to work with the party that submitted the Informal Challenge (or its representative)
     toward a resolution of the challenge. If PGE disagrees with such challenge, PGE will
     provide the Interested Party(ies) with an explanation supporting the inputs, supporting
     explanations, allocations, calculations, or other information. No Informal Challenge may
     be submitted after January 31, and PGE must respond to all Informal Challenges by no
     later than February 28, unless the Review Period is extended by PGE or FERC.

C.   Informal Challenges shall be subject to the resolution procedures and limitations in this
     Section IV. Formal Challenges shall be filed pursuant to these protocols and shall satisfy
     all of the following requirements.

     1.     A Formal Challenge shall:

            a.      Clearly identify the action or inaction which is alleged to violate the filed
                    rate formula or protocols;

            b.      Explain how the action or inaction violates the filed rate formula or
                    protocols;

            c.      Set forth the business, commercial, economic or other issues presented
                    by the action or inaction as such relate to or affect the party filing the
                    Formal Challenge, including:

                     i.     The extent or effect of an Accounting Change;

                    ii.     Whether the Annual True-Up or PTRR fails to include data
                            properly recorded in accordance with these protocols;

                   iii.     The proper application of the formula rate and procedures in these
                            protocols;

                   iv.      The accuracy of data and consistency with the formula rate of the
                            charges shown in the Annual True-Up or PTRR;

                    v.      The prudence of actual costs and expenditures;

                                               6
                   vi.       The effect of any change to the underlying Uniform System of
                            Accounts or FERC Form No. 1;

                  vii.      The prudence of procurement methods and cost control
                            methodologies used by PGE; or

                 viii.      Any other information that may reasonably have substantive effect
                            on the calculation of the charge pursuant to the formula.

            d.      Make a good faith effort to quantify the financial impact or burden (if
                    any) created for the party filing the Formal Challenge as a result of the
                    action or inaction;

            e.      State whether the issues presented are pending in an existing Commission
                    proceeding or a proceeding in any other forum in which the filing party
                    is a party, and if so, provide an explanation why timely resolution cannot
                    be achieved in that forum;

            f.      State the specific relief or remedy requested, including any request for
                    stay or extension of time, and the basis for that relief;

            g.      Include all documents that support the facts in the Formal Challenge in
                    possession of, or otherwise attainable by, the filing party, including, but
                    not limited to, contracts and affidavits; and

            h.      State whether the filing party utilized the Informal Challenge procedures
                    described in these protocols to dispute the action or inaction raised by the
                    Formal Challenge, and, if not, describe why not.

     2.     Service. Any person filing a Formal Challenge must serve a copy of the Formal
            Challenge on PGE. Service to PGE must be simultaneous with filing at the
            Commission. Simultaneous service can be accomplished by electronic mail in
            accordance with § 385.2010(f)(3), facsimile, express delivery, or messenger. The
            party filing the Formal Challenge shall serve the individual listed as the contact
            person on PGE’s Informational Filing required under Section VI of these
            protocols.

D.   Informal and Formal Challenges shall be limited to all issues that may be necessary to
     determine: (1) the extent or effect of an Accounting Change; (2) whether the Annual
     True-Up or PTRR fails to include data properly recorded in accordance with these
     protocols; (3) the proper application of the formula rate and procedures in these
     protocols; (4) the accuracy of data and consistency with the formula rate of the
     calculations shown in the Annual True-Up and PTRR; (5) the prudence of actual costs
     and expenditures; (6) the prudence of procurement methods and cost control
     methodologies used by PGE; (7) the effect of any change to the underlying Uniform
     System of Accounts or FERC Form No. 1; or (8) any other information that may
     reasonably have substantive effect on the calculation of the Annual True-Up and PTRR


                                              7
      pursuant to the formula.

E.   PGE will cause to be posted all Informal Challenges from Interested Parties and PGE’s
     response(s) to such Informal Challenges; except, however, if Informal Challenges or
     responses to Informal Challenges include material deemed by PGE to be confidential
     information, such information will not be publicly posted but will be made available to
     requesting parties pursuant to a confidentiality agreement to be executed by PGE and
     the requesting party.

F.   Any changes or adjustments to the True-Up Adjustment or PTRR resulting from the
     Information Exchange and Informal Challenge processes that are agreed to by PGE
     will be reported in the Informational Filing required pursuant to Section VI of these
     protocols. Any such changes or adjustments agreed to by PGE on or before December
     1 will be reflected in the PTRR for the upcoming Rate Year. Any changes or
     adjustments agreed to by PGE after December 1 will be reflected in the following
     year’s Annual True-Up, as discussed in Section V of these protocols.

G.   An Interested Party shall have until April 15 following the Review Period (unless such
     date is extended with the written consent of PGE to continue efforts to resolve the
     Informal Challenge) to make a Formal Challenge with FERC, which shall be served on
     PGE on the date of such filing as specified in Section IV.C(2) above. A Formal
     Challenge shall be filed in the same docket as PGE’s Informational Filing discussed in
     Section VI of these protocols. PGE shall respond to the Formal Challenge by the
     deadline established by FERC. A party may pursue a Formal Challenge with respect to
     one or more issues within the scope of Section IV.D above provided the party submitted
     an Informal Challenge during the applicable Review Period with respect any issue,
     which need not be the same as the issue or issues raised in the Formal Challenge.

H.   In any proceeding initiated by FERC concerning the Annual True-Up or PTRR or in
     response to a Formal Challenge, PGE shall bear the burden, consistent with section 205
     of the Federal Power Act, of proving that it has correctly applied the terms of the
     formula rate consistent with these protocols, and that it followed the applicable
     requirements and procedures. Nothing herein is intended to alter the burdens applied by
     FERC with respect to prudence challenges.

I.   Except as specifically provided herein, nothing herein shall be deemed to limit in any way
     the right of PGE to file unilaterally, pursuant to Federal Power Act section 205 and the
     regulations thereunder, to change the formula rate or any of its inputs (including, but not
     limited to, rate of return and transmission incentive rate treatment), or to replace the
     formula rate with a stated rate, or the right of any other party to request such changes
     pursuant to section 206 of the Federal Power Act and the regulations thereunder.

J.   No party shall seek to modify the formula rate under the Challenge Procedures set forth
     in these protocols, and the Annual True-Up and PTRR shall not be subject to challenge
     by anyone for the purpose of modifying the formula rate. Any modifications to the
     formula rate will require, as applicable, a Federal Power Act section 205 or section 206
     filing.

                                              8
 K.     Any Interested Party seeking changes to the application of the formula rate due to a
       change in the Uniform System of Accounts or FERC Form No. 1, shall first raise
       the matter with PGE in accordance with this Section IV before pursuing a Formal
       Challenge.

Section V.     Changes to True-Up Adjustment or Projected Net Revenue Requirement

Except as provided in Section IV.F of these protocols, any rate changes as the result of any
FERC proceeding to consider the Annual True-Up or PTRR, or as a result of the procedures set
forth herein, shall be incorporated into the formula rate and the charges produced by the formula
rate in the PTRR for the next Rate Year. This reconciliation mechanism shall apply in lieu of
mid-Rate Year adjustments. Interest on any refund or surcharge shall be calculated in
accordance with the procedures outlined in Section VII of these protocols.

Section VI.    Informational Filings

A.     By March 15 of each year subsequent to calendar year 2027, PGE shall submit to FERC
       an informational filing (“Informational Filing”) of its PTRR for the Rate Year, including
       its Annual True-Up and True-Up Adjustment.2 Within 10 days of submitting the
       Informational Filing, PGE shall provide notice of such submission via an email exploder
       list. This Informational Filing must include the information that is reasonably necessary
       to determine: (1) that input data under the formula rate are properly recorded in any
       underlying workpapers; (2) that PGE has properly applied the formula rate and these
       procedures; (3) the accuracy of data and the consistency with the formula rate of the
       Transmission Revenue Requirement and rates under review; (4) the extent of accounting
       changes that affect formula rate inputs; and (5) the reasonableness of projected costs. The
       Informational Filing must also describe any corrections or adjustments made during that
       period, and must describe all aspects of the formula rate or its inputs that are the subject
       of an ongoing dispute under the Informal or Formal Challenge procedures.

B.     Any challenges to the implementation of the Formula Rate must be made through the
       Challenge Procedures described in Section IV of these protocols. Alternatively, FERC
       or any entity may at any time file a complaint under Section 206 of the Federal Power
       Act concerning the Formula Rate and/or its implementation, and nothing in these
       Protocols precludes the submission of such a complaint.

C.     Finally, the Informational Filing shall include for the applicable Rate Year the following
       information related to affiliate cost allocation: a detailed description of the methodologies
       used to allocate and directly assign costs between PGE and its affiliates by service
       category or function, including any changes to such cost allocation methodologies from
       the prior Rate Year, and the reasons and justification for those changes; the magnitude of
       such costs that have been allocated or directly assigned between PGE and each affiliate by
       service category or function; and a copy of any service agreement between PGE and any


2
      The March 15, 2028 Informational Filing will not include information related to an
Annual True-Up and True-Up Adjustment because those calculations will not occur until June 1,
2028.
                                                 9
        affiliate that went into effect during the Rate Year.

Section VII. Calculation of True-Up Adjustment

The True-Up Adjustment will be determined in the following manner:

       1.      Actual transmission revenues received the previous Rate Year (“True-Up Year”)
               shall be compared to the ATRR for the True-Up Year as determined using PGE’s
               completed FERC Form No. 1 report to determine any excess or shortfall. The
               excess or shortfall due to the actual revenue received versus the ATRR shall
               constitute the “True-Up Adjustment.” The True-Up Adjustment and related
               calculations shall be posted to PGE’s OASIS no later than June 1 each year
               subsequent to calendar year 2027 (or if that day falls on a weekend or a holiday
               recognized by FERC, then the posting shall be due on the next business day)
               following the issuance of the FERC Form No. 1 for the previous year, as set forth
               in Section II of these protocols.

       2.      Interest on any under or over recovery of the net revenue requirement shall be
               determined based on the Commission’s regulation at 18 C.F.R § 35.19a. The
               interest payable shall be calculated using an average interest rate for the twenty-
               four (24) months during which the over or under recovery in the revenue
               requirement exists. The interest rate to be applied to the over or under recovery
               amounts will be determined using the average rate for the twenty (20) months
               preceding September of the current year. The interest amount will be included in
               the projected costs made available on September 1, as described in Section II.C
               above.

       3.      The Net Revenue Requirement for transmission services for the following Rate
               Year shall be the sum of the PTRR for the following year, plus or minus the True-
               Up Adjustment from the True-Up Year, if any, including interest, as explained
               above.

       4.      PGE may accelerate the refund of any over recovery amounts by one year. The
               interest calculation will be adjusted to reflect the period the over recovery exists.

Section I.    Applicability

The following procedures shall apply to Portland General Electric Company’s (“PGE”)
calculation of its actual net transmission revenue requirement (“ATRR”), True-Up Adjustment,
and projected net transmission revenue requirement (“PTRR”).

Section II.   Annual True-Up and Projected Net Revenue Requirement

A.     On or before June 1 of each year subsequent to calendar year 2027, PGE shall
       determine its Annual True-Up pursuant to its Formula Rate template and Section VII
       of these protocols, to derive a True-Up Adjustment to be included in PGE’s PTRR for
       the subsequent calendar year (the “Rate Year”).

B.     On or before June 1 of each year subsequent to calendar year 2027, PGE shall provide its
       Annual True-Up, ATRR, and True-Up Adjustment and cause such information to be
       posted on OASIS.

C.     On or before September 1 of each year, PGE shall provide its PTRR and cause such
       information to be posted on OASIS. PGE will conduct a meeting with Interested Parties
       (as such term is defined in Section II.G of these protocols) on the PTRR for the Rate
       Year within thirty (30) days of posting. Notice of the customer meeting, including the
       time, date, and location, shall be posted on OASIS and distributed to the e-mail exploder
       list no less than seven (7) days prior to such meeting.

D.     If the date for posting the Annual True-Up or the PTRR falls on a weekend or a holiday
       recognized by FERC, then the posting shall be due on the next business day. The date on
       which posting of the Annual True-Up occurs shall be that year’s “Publication Date.” Any
       delay in the Publication Date or in the posting of the PTRR will result in an equivalent
       extension of time for the submission of Information Requests discussed in Section III of
       these protocols.

E.     The Annual True-Up shall:

        1.    Include a workable data-populated Formula Rate Template and underlying
              workpapers in native format with all formulas and links intact;

        2.    Be based on PGE’s FERC Form No. 1 for the prior calendar year;

        3.    Provide the formula rate calculations and all inputs thereto, as well as supporting
